kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the source panels and the AGONIST WITH table.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid supplies the three curve panels and the four-row table; the attack structure is a KYP design.

kypExtensions.summary: The two-question reading (WHICH COLUMN MOVED? potency ↓ = right shift = competitive; efficacy ↓ = ceiling drop = noncompetitive OR partial agonist; efficacy NEGATIVE = below baseline = inverse agonist — and potency 'Independent' marks the partial agonist's EC50 as free to sit anywhere. IS IT SURMOUNTABLE? the REMARKS column's single test — 'Can be overcome by ↑ agonist concentration' = competitive; 'Cannot be overcome by ↑ agonist concentration' = noncompetitive — turning the table's POTENCY/EFFICACY/REMARKS columns into one decision protocol for any drug-pair stem) — KYP's synthesis of the page's three panels and four table rows into a single reading order (parameter moved → surmountability → row identity).
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints three panels and a four-row table as parallel blocks without a unified reading protocol; the which-column/which-parameter framing and the surmountability-first test are KYP's design.

kypExtensions.summary: The four KYP mnemonics (1 — COMPETITIVE SLIDES RIGHT, SAME CEILING: surmountable, potency ↓, efficacy unchanged; 2 — NONCOMPETITIVE CLIPS THE CEILING, SAME SPOT: insurmountable, efficacy ↓, potency unchanged; 3 — PARTIALS SHARE THE SITE, DROP THE CEILING: same site as the full agonist, efficacy ↓, potency independent; 4 — INVERSE GOES NEGATIVE: needs a constitutively active receptor, efficacy below the neutral-antagonist baseline). The Receptor binding section prints NO margin mnemonic — the page's only printed mnemonic ('TITE') belongs to the EXCLUDED Therapeutic index section — so all four codes are KYP-original designs.
kypExtensions.rationale: Book 233's Receptor binding section prints NO mnemonic; all four codes are KYP-original designs.

notes: Census (pdfimages + VLM): NO raster images on the page (pdfimages -list returned zero rows for pdf 255). The Receptor binding section is typeset text plus three vector curve panels: the AGONIST WITH table (text layer) and the three dose-response panels (vector line-art curves with text labels — drawn curves, not photographs). The table prints in the text layer and is carried verbatim in the note's table blocks and re-typeset in the registry visual's table grid (ORIGINAL_KYP_ADAPTATION) — short attributed definition sentences and drug pairs, not artwork reproductions. The three curve panels are redrawn as ORIGINAL_KYP_REDRAW vector line-art sigmoids in the registry visual (competitive right shift; noncompetitive Emax reduction; two partial agonists — one at the agonist's EC50 with reduced efficacy, one shifted with independent potency) — the curve shapes are the standard Hill sigmoids of pharmacodynamics, re-drawn from scratch; no copyrighted artwork is reproduced. The Receptor binding section prints NO margin mnemonic (the page's only printed mnemonic, 'TITE', lives in the EXCLUDED Therapeutic index section); the KYP memory layer adds four original codes (COMPETITIVE SLIDES RIGHT, NONCOMPETITIVE CLIPS THE CEILING, PARTIALS SHARE THE SITE, INVERSE GOES NEGATIVE). No copyrighted photographs exist on the page; nothing reproduced. EXCLUSION: the 'Therapeutic index' section opens on this SAME page (lower half) — its header, 'Measurement of drug safety.', the TD50/ED50 equation, the therapeutic-window definition, the 'TITE' mnemonic, the low-TI drug list (warfarin, theophylline, digoxin, antiepileptic drugs, lithium), the LD50 note, and the Efficacy/Toxicity quantal-curve panel are ALL excluded from this topic: they belong to the separate pending topic PH9 (therapeutic-index), which pins the same source page (pdf 255 / book 233).
